Senses.Explanation: A formulaic “take care.” In recorded sayings a master ends a hall address, informal convocation, address to the assembly, or whisk talk with it and steps down. Recurrent formulas include “You have stood long, kind assembly; I humbly hope you take care; he stepped down,” and the shorter “Take care; he then stepped down.” It is also a parting word in dialogue: a departing monk says “take care” and leaves. A written final statement closes, “I humbly hope you take care” (伏惟珍重), before its author puts down the brush and asks whether to depart sitting or lying. This leave-taking formula is a separate speech act from the transitive verb “to treasure” an object.
Senses.Note: Primary corpus deployment: a formulaic close and parting word, not a specialized technical term. The curated passages show a whisk talk, a hall address, an address to the assembly, and a monk's farewell. The headword has 3,863 hits in 351 allowlisted texts; this high-frequency formula is distinct from the rarer transitive verb.

Occurrences.Kwic: 久立眾慈，伏惟珍重。下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Guiding Principles from the Patriarchs: the formula closes a whisk talk at the end of a retreat; the assembly is dismissed and the master steps down.
Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters: the word closes a hall address in the short formula “Take care; he then stepped down.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 與大眾舉一古人方便。珍重便下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde-era Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, section on the heirs of Guichen: after raising an old worthy's expedient, the speaker says “take care” and steps down.
Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fenyang Wude: in dialogue, a monk says “take care” and leaves; Fenyang then supplies an alternate reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今吾如是，豈不快哉！塵勞外緣，一時掃盡。荷諸山垂顧，咸願證明。伏惟珍重。置筆顧簡堂曰：某坐去好，臥去好？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A written final statement thanks the assembled mountain masters, closes 'I humbly hope you take care,' and is followed by the writer putting down the brush and asking whether to depart sitting or lying.

Senses.Explanation: A transitive verb meaning to treasure or value an object. Letters and prefaces record “treasure the teaching gate” (珍重法門), “treasure this record and circulate it widely” (珍重此錄，廣為流佈), and “if [you] wish to value that matter” (若欲珍重其事). Unlike the stock closing “take care,” these clauses name what is valued.
Senses.Note: The three independently sourced objects establish the distinct action of valuing something, not merely a grammatical variant or interpretation of the leave-taking formula. No special Chan deviation beyond the corpus objects is asserted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 屢承翰教，珍重法門，筆舌難盡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A letter says that its addressee treasures the teaching gate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又能珍重此錄，廣為流佈
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A preface praises treasuring this record and circulating it widely.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若欲珍重其事，且放過諸人一著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A hall address uses the headword transitively of valuing that matter.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, a repeated, layered, or weighty barrier. The expression occurs 739 times in 227 allowlisted texts. Counts range from one to ten thousand barriers; one passes, breaks, opens, guards, or remains separated by them. The recurring warning says, ‘do not say no-mind is the Way; no-mind still leaves one further barrier.’ Speakers also ask who has passed it, request presentation of ‘the final barrier,’ and direct a questioner to ‘ask the gatekeeper.’ A late discourse gives its own named description of ‘passing through the further barrier’; this is preserved as that text’s account, not made universal. Zen bends the checkpoint image into a public measure, but the corpus names no fixed numbered stage shared by every use.
Senses.Note: Family check: “one further barrier” (一重關), “two barriers” (兩重關), “four barriers” (四重關), “a thousand and ten thousand barriers” (千重萬重), “the final formidable barrier” (末後重關), “the buddhas’ and patriarchs’ formidable barrier” (佛祖重關), and “pass through the formidable barrier” (透重關) vary scale or sequence, not referent. No split.

Occurrences.Kwic: 莫謂無心云是道，無心猶隔一重關。示眾，云：泥佛不度水，木佛不度火，金佛不度爐，真佛內裏坐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The repeated warning presents no-mind as still separated by one further barrier.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：木馬衝開千騎路，鐵牛透過萬重關。木馬鐵牛，即今在甚麼處？良久曰：驚起暮天沙上雁，海門斜去兩三行
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The iron ox passes through ten thousand barriers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「如何過得這重關？」師云：「問取把關吏。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A question asks how to pass it; the answer names the gatekeeper.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「大開爐煹，鋾鑄聖凡，末後重關，請師拈出。」師云：「但得雪消後，自然春到來。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk requests presentation of the final barrier.

Occurrences.Kwic: 境智融通，色空無礙，獲大自在，常住不動，是則名為透重關，名為大死大活者。透重關後，家舍即在途中，途中不離家舍
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A late text gives an explicit formula for what it calls passing the barrier.

Occurrences.Kwic: 眾中莫有透出重關者麼？出來與華藏相見。良久，云：無人知此意，令我憶南泉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public challenge asks whether anyone has passed it.
